title: The fresher who will not miss his exam
name: Samir
description: First-year engineering student, six weeks into halls. Was at a music festival at the weekend and has an exam on Thursday he has already resat once. His flatmate carried him down three flights of stairs to the taxi.
personality: Polite, apologetic, and frightened underneath it. Keeps apologising for wasting your time. Very focused on getting out in time for his exam. Will answer straight if you ask him straight.
symptoms: my head is splitting and nothing touches it
the strip light in here is unbearable
I cannot get warm, my hands and feet are freezing
everything aches, my legs most of all
I have been sick twice in the taxi
lie: It is just a heat rash from the festival. It has been there for days.
truth: The marks came up this evening and there are more of them than there were an hour ago. I did not want to say because I am terrified of what it means.
cracks_when: pressed on it a second time, or asked what his flatmate noticed
red_herrings: blames it all on the festival and four nights of no sleep
everyone in halls has had a bug this month
key_questions: does the light hurt your eyes

canned.does the light hurt your eyes: Can you turn it off? It goes right through me.
canned.is your neck stiff: I cannot get my chin anywhere near my chest. It has seized up.
canned.when did this start: Yesterday afternoon I felt off. By midnight I could not stand up.
canned._greeting: Sorry to be here at this hour. I think I just need fluids.
canned._whats_wrong: A bad bug, I assume. Everyone in halls has had one.
_deflect: It is the festival catching up with me.
I have an exam Thursday. I cannot be in here.
Half of halls has had this. I will be fine by morning.
Sorry, can you say that again? I cannot think straight.
canned._feeling: Cold. Really cold, and my head is splitting.

exam.general: Drowsy but rousable. Cold, mottled peripheries with a capillary refill of 4 seconds. Looks unwell at the end of the bed.
exam.skin: Non-blanching purpuric spots over both shins and the left flank, several larger than 2mm. More visible now than on arrival.
exam.neurological: Photophobia and marked neck stiffness. Kernig's positive. No focal deficit. GCS 14.
exam.cognition: Oriented to person and place but not to time. Slow to answer.
exam.cardiovascular: Tachycardic 124, thready. BP 102/58 and falling. Cold to the knees.
exam.eyes: Pupils equal and reactive. Marked photophobia on examination.
exam.legs: Purpuric spots over both shins. Severe myalgia on passive movement.

level_card: Nineteen, three in the morning, and desperate to be gone by Thursday.
He has a headache, a stiff neck and cold hands.
Look at his legs. Then look again a minute later.
reveal_note: The marks were not a heat rash, and there were more of them every time anyone looked.
opening_line: Sorry to be here at this hour. I think I just need fluids.

presentation.duration: Yesterday afternoon I felt off. By midnight I could not stand up
presentation.triage_note: Carried in by flatmate. Febrile, photophobic, neck stiffness, cold peripheries. Marks noted on shins.

past_medical: Nothing. I have never been properly ill
medications: I took paracetamol earlier, it did nothing
social: First year engineering, I live in halls
I was at a festival at the weekend
I drink a bit at weekends like everyone

harmful_treatments.nsaid: He is shutting down his kidneys already. An NSAID here makes that worse and treats nothing that matters.
harmful_treatments.benzodiazepine_sedation: Drowsiness here is the illness, not agitation. Sedating him removes your only neurological observation.

management_points: Antibiotics first, within the hour, and before any imaging or lumbar puncture
Blood cultures before antibiotics only if it costs no delay at all
Fluid resuscitation for shock, reassessing after each bolus
A non-blanching rash with fever is sepsis until proven otherwise; test it with a glass
Lumbar puncture only once he is stable and coagulation is known, never before antibiotics
Critical care review early: cold peripheries and a falling pressure in a teenager decompensate late and fast
Notify public health and arrange contact prophylaxis for his household

teaching.summary: A 19-year-old with headache, photophobia, neck stiffness and a spreading non-blanching rash, who is trying to be discharged in time for an exam. Cold peripheries and a four-second refill say he is already shocked.
pearls: Antibiotics before imaging, before the lumbar puncture, before anything.
A rash that is spreading while you watch it is the whole diagnosis.
Teenagers compensate beautifully and then fall off a cliff.
Cold hands and a normal blood pressure is shock, not reassurance.
Ask the friend who brought them in what has changed in the last hour.

key_question_reasons: A rash that does not blanch, in a teenager who is unwell, is meningococcal sepsis until proven otherwise. Nothing else comes first.
Photophobia with fever points at meningitis rather than a simple viral illness.
Neck stiffness completes the picture, though it is often absent early -- its absence excludes nothing.
Hours, not days. Meningococcal disease moves faster than almost anything else you will see, and the timeline drives how fast you must.
